title: Simplification: Council gives final green light to new laws boosting defence industry and readiness
key_claim: On 9 October 2026 the Council gave final approval to three acts (Omnibus V); the directive on intra-EU transfers and defence procurement introduces two new mandatory general transfer licences, one for certified suppliers and recipients and one for intra-EU industrial partnerships; the acts enter into force on the twentieth day after publication.
frame_summary: The Council presents the omnibus as a package that removes administrative delay from defence procurement, permitting and transfers, with the two general transfer licences as the transfer measure.
verbatim_quote: introduces two new mandatory general transfer licences
verbatim_list: It sets the maximum duration of the permit-granting process at 102 working days.
will enter into force on the twentieth day following that of their publication
notes: WebFetch 21/10/2026; dateline '9 October 2026 10:20', page last reviewed 14 October. Council press release about its own act; the act text itself (PE-CONS 46/26) is the second source.

title: PE-CONS 46/26: Directive simplifying intra-EU transfers of defence-related products and security and defence procurement (final text)
key_claim: The final text makes the new general transfer licence conditional on the recipient and supplier both being undertakings certified under Article 9; certification is judged on proven experience in defence transfers and export activities, among other criteria; the text sets no day or month limit for deciding a certification application; Member States adopt measures 12 months after entry into force and apply them 15 months after it; a separate licence covers structured intra-EU industrial partnerships.
frame_summary: The act text allocates the faster transfer route by certification status and track record, and sets application dates for the licences but no date or deadline for certifying firms.
verbatim_quote: the recipient and the supplier are undertakings certified in accordance with Article 9
verbatim_list: proven experience in defence transfers and export activities
Certified undertakings have demonstrated strong capacity to comply with transfer and export control rules
have also supported important costs to achieve certification

notes: WebFetch 21/10/2026 of the PE-CONS PDF (cover 'Brussels, 23 September 2026'). The 'no time limit for deciding a certification application' finding rests on the amended provisions reproduced in the act; unamended parts of Article 9 are not reproduced there, so the body words it as 'the amended text sets no deadline'.

title: Omnibus V: Defence readiness (At a glance)
key_claim: Parliament's research service describes the provisional agreement as introducing two mandatory general transfer licences, one for certified suppliers and recipients, and says it does not detail the certification criteria.
frame_summary: EPRS summarises the omnibus deal for Members and treats certification as the basis of one transfer licence while leaving the criteria to the legal texts.
verbatim_quote: introduces two mandatory general transfer licences
notes: WebFetch 21/10/2026. Explanatory note for Members; does not represent an official Parliament position. Used to corroborate the licence pair.

title: The Defence of Europe in a New Era: An Assessment (Strategic Dossier)
date_evidence: First published September 2026 by The International Institute for Strategic Studies.
key_claim: IISS says European firms that find new suppliers and alternative materials are faced with costly and lengthy recertification processes, and quotes Commissioner Kubilius that the absence of a single European market for defence continues to present major obstacles to large-scale defence-industrial production.
frame_summary: IISS argues that European defence output is held back by fragmentation and qualification friction, not only by money.

title: Two Licences and a Qualification Threshold
key_claim: The faster transfer category depends on which undertakings qualify, a question the compromise leaves open; it reads the licences against fifty-five certified undertakings counted in the Commission's 2016 evaluation (fourteen in Germany, twelve in France, half the Member States none); citing a Commission staff working document of 3 November 2025, a general licence typically allows a transfer within one to three days against six to seven weeks for a simple individual licence.
frame_summary: The newsletter argues that the two new licences speed transfers only for firms that clear the qualification test, which the political deal did not settle.
verbatim_quote: Which undertakings will be able to enter the faster category at all is the question the compromise leaves open.
verbatim_list: The figure against which those instruments have to be read is fifty-five, the number of certified undertakings the Commission counted across the Union in its 2016 evaluation of the transfers directive, fourteen of them in Germany and twelve in France, with half the Member States holding none.

licence typically allows a transfer to be performed within one to three days, whereas the average time for authorities to process a simple individual transfer licence can be estimated at six to seven weeks.

title: Neue Allgemeine Genehmigungen: BMWE sorgt für spürbare Erleichterungen bei Kriegswaffentransporten und -handelsgeschäften
key_claim: Germany's amended general-authorisation ordinance for war weapons took effect on 8 September 2026 and adds a general authorisation for intra-Community shipments between certified undertakings in different EU Member States.
frame_summary: A German law firm reports that Germany's own new general authorisations also tie the fastest intra-EU shipping route to certified undertakings.
verbatim_quote: Drittens besteht nun auch eine allgemeine Genehmigung für innergemeinschaftliche Verbringungen zwischen zertifizierten Unternehmen in unterschiedlichen EU-Mitgliedstaaten
notes: WebFetch 21/10/2026. Law-firm newsletter (Oppenhoff, Cologne). German-language source for the German national layer.

title: Offener Brief warnt: EU droht Kontrolle über Waffenexporte zu verlieren
key_claim: A coalition of 25 civil society organisations warned that wider general transfer licences would leave authorities unable to monitor the end-use of a considerable share of their transfers.
frame_summary: Civil society argues the omnibus risks making the fast lane too wide for authorities to police, the opposite worry to the scan's.
